docs.title: BRIDGE Measurements hackathon, 2026-09-30: synthesis and first-pass module
docs.text:
At the 2026-09-30 BRIDGE Data Modeling - Measurement Metadata Hackathon, the group agreed to build a straw-person schema from the transcript, the brainstorm drawing and the draft module, then see whether each source can map up to it. This page is that synthesis. The schema is src/ber_central_schema/schema/measurements.yaml version 0.5.0 (see "What changed in 0.5.0" and "What changed in 0.4.0"). The full list of what was raised, with where each item went, is measurements-hackathon/raised-items.md.

Inputs:

  • Hackathon Notes, main tab and Report Out tab: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1_MTh8PRRG5cn2DV-b8wr9u8bu_EmChAHREfhUX4Ks9I
  • The hackathon Zoom chat, saved locally by one attendee (not published)
  • The "measurement brainstorm" drawing: https://docs.google.com/drawings/d/1llZ1wNabHL1A1EXYxelY62qru8Qz1tdaDvT2pdvW50Y
  • The intro slides: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1-2ai8pYpBnytDB8-ihF4e1pK2RoUW2zGDxgOMUsPqHE
  • The example data each organization put in the hackathon shared drive (JGI, NMDC, EMSL, ORNL)
  • https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/issues/4, GOLD organism measurements mapped to BRIDGE measurement draft 0.2.0
  • The 10/07/2026 entry in the BRIDGE DM weekly notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ezgBR6IbJNJjDntK27djICFIFNBKHeNtdgHqwELMQqU
  • Added 2026-10-12: @dschristianson's review of this PR, 2026-10-09, 13 inline comments: https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#pullrequestreview-5470820043
  • Added 2026-10-12: https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/issues/11, Attribute/value representation (@ialarmedalien, 2026-10-09)

The meeting transcript was not available when this was written, and none had been found as of 2026-10-12. BASALT and KBase presented but left no files in the shared drive, so their examples here come from the slides and the 0.2.0 module. ESS-DIVE has since shared example data privately (2026-10-07), and @dschristianson is testing the model against it; none of it is used or described here.

docs.title: What the group agreed
docs.text:
• Start with one class and add structure only when data needs it (@mslarae13 in the drawing; the 10/07 notes "slightly leaning towards one concept for now").
  • A measurement needs a type, a value, a raw value and a unit (10/07 notes).
  • Keep the source text, and parse numbers, ranges and units beside it (@valerie-autumn-skye, JGI notes).
  • Parse and normalize once after ingest, rather than leaving it to every agent on every query (@ialarmedalien, with agreement from @sierra-moxon and @dschristianson in the chat). That is an ETL decision; the schema gives the parsed values a place to go.
  • Make the schema, then map each source up to it, with a feedback loop up to a cutoff date (@corilo, @turbomam).

docs.title: Terms
docs.text:
This page, the schema and review replies use these terms with these meanings.

  • Measurement: one value of one property of one thing, as a source reported it. It is the Measurement class. A measurement may carry a number, a range, a term, only the source text, or a reason no value is present.
  • Observation: the SOSA class sosa:Observation, which Measurement is close-mapped to. This page uses "observation" only for that class and in open question 1, which asks how a measurement relates to an observation. There is no Observation class in this schema yet.
  • https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-ssn/#SOSAObservation
  • Attribute: the Attribute class proposed in https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/12, a source's key and value attached to another record. How Measurement relates to Attribute is open in https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/issues/11.
  • Entity-attribute-value (EAV) model: each value is its own record that names the thing described and the property given, rather than a slot named for the property on a class for that thing. Measurement follows this model.
  • https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entity%E2%80%93attribute%E2%80%93value_model
  • Feature of interest: the thing whose property was measured, in feature_of_interest.
  • https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-ssn/#SOSAFeatureOfInterest
  • Observed property: the property that was measured, in observed_property, as a bridge_property: term. The name follows SOSA's sosa:observedProperty; a measured property is the same thing.
  • https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-ssn/#SOSAobservedProperty
  • Term: one entry in src/ber_central_schema/terms/bridge_property.tsv, with an ID, a label and a definition. The ID does not change once merged; the label and definition can be edited.

docs.title: The first-pass model
docs.text:
One class, Measurement. Every slot except the property is optional, but a measurement must name its property and carry at least one value or a reason it has none.

classDiagram
    class Measurement {
        what was measured
        observed_property : uriorcurie
        property_label : string
        feature_of_interest : uriorcurie
        the value
        raw_value : string
        numeric_value : double
        minimum_numeric_value : double
        maximum_numeric_value : double
        unit : UCUM code, ASCII
        unit_basis : string
        coded_value : uriorcurie
        comparator : ComparatorEnum
        statistic : StatisticEnum
        standard_deviation : double
        sample_size : integer
        value_role : ValueRoleEnum
        value_qualifier : ValueQualifierEnum
        missing_value_reason : MissingValueReasonEnum
        how and when
        measurement_method : string
        treatment : string
        instrument : string
        observed_time : PartialDateTime
        observed_start_time : PartialDateTime
        observed_end_time : PartialDateTime
        where it came from
        measurement_id : uriorcurie
        source_system : string
        source_record_id : string
        source_field : string
        quality_flag : string
    }
    class ValueRoleEnum {
        measured
        setting
        interpreted
        derived
    }
    class ValueQualifierEnum {
        optimum
        tolerated
    }
    class MissingValueReasonEnum {
        not_determined
        not_applicable
        not_reported
        below_detection_limit
        above_detection_limit
        unknown
        out_of_range
    }
    class ComparatorEnum {
        less_than
        less_than_or_equal
        greater_than
        greater_than_or_equal
        approximately
    }
    class StatisticEnum {
        mean
        median
        minimum
        maximum
        standard_deviation
        sum
    }
    Measurement --> ValueRoleEnum
    Measurement --> ValueQualifierEnum
    Measurement --> MissingValueReasonEnum
    Measurement --> ComparatorEnum
    Measurement --> StatisticEnum

The rules the schema enforces, each with a counter-example in tests/data/invalid:

Rule Counter-example Name the property with exactly one of observed_property or property_label Measurement-001, Measurement-008, Measurement-009 Carry at least one of raw_value, numeric_value, minimum_numeric_value, maximum_numeric_value, coded_value or missing_value_reason Measurement-003 unit is printable ASCII (um, not µm) Measurement-002 numeric_value is a number Measurement-004 comparator comes from its enum Measurement-005 sample_size is at least 1 Measurement-006 standard_deviation is not negative Measurement-007 observed_time and the start and end times are ISO 8601 at year, month, date or date-time resolution, and a time of day carries a UTC offset; months, days, hours and minutes must be in range Measurement-010, Measurement-011, Measurement-012

docs.title: How a messy source value becomes measurements
docs.text:
A source cell can hold more than one value. The parser splits it into one record per value, every record keeps the whole original cell in raw_value, and they share source_record_id and source_field. This GOLD pressure cell is tests/data/valid/Measurement-005.yaml and Measurement-006.yaml:

flowchart LR
    cell["GOLD Go0120212, organism_pressure:<br/>0–30 MPa (Optimal 10MPa)"]
    cell --> a["Measurement<br/>observed_property: bridge_property:pressure<br/>minimum_numeric_value: 0<br/>maximum_numeric_value: 30<br/>unit: MPa<br/>value_qualifier: tolerated"]
    cell --> b["Measurement<br/>observed_property: bridge_property:pressure<br/>numeric_value: 10<br/>unit: MPa<br/>value_qualifier: optimum"]

Values that cannot be parsed are kept, not dropped:

flowchart TD
    v["Source value"] --> q1{"Can it be parsed?"}
    q1 -- "a number" --> n["numeric_value + unit"]
    q1 -- "a range" --> r["minimum_numeric_value + maximum_numeric_value + unit"]
    q1 -- "mean, SD, n" --> s["numeric_value + statistic + standard_deviation + sample_size"]
    q1 -- "a category" --> c["raw_value + value_role: interpreted (+ coded_value when a reviewed term exists)"]
    q1 -- "says there is no value" --> m["raw_value + missing_value_reason"]
    q1 -- "no" --> f["raw_value + quality_flag: needs_review"]

docs.title: How a measurement names its property
docs.text:
Every measurement names its observed property with a bridge_property: term ID, or with free text in property_label when no term exists yet. Each term has an ID, a label and a definition in src/ber_central_schema/terms/bridge_property.tsv. Mappings to BERVO, MIxS, METPO and other vocabularies live in src/ber_central_schema/mappings/observed_property.sssom.tsv, not on each measurement. New terms are added by pull request, and a term's ID does not change once merged. When BERVO lacks a term, it is requested from BERVO (for example https://github.com/bioepic-data/bervo/issues/207).

flowchart LR
    p["Property of a source value"] --> i{"BRIDGE property ID exists?"}
    i -- yes --> bp["observed_property: bridge_property:..."]
    i -- no --> l["property_label: free text"]
    bp --> m["observed_property.sssom.tsv<br/>bervo:, MIXS: and METPO: mappings"]

Each source's own table, from its field names to bridge_property: IDs and from its unit spellings to UCUM codes, belongs with that source (as SSSOM in the source's repository), linked from the source's entry in https://github.com/doe-bridge/lakehouse-registry, rather than in this repository.

property_label is the catch-all for values that fit nowhere else. It plays the same part as MIxS misc_param (MIXS:0000752), NMDC's PropertyAssertion, BERtron's Attribute and the feature model's Attribute. All four allow a free-text key when no identifier exists. tests/data/valid/Measurement-020.yaml is the MIxS and NMDC misc_param example (bicarbonate) as a Measurement.

docs.title: What changed in 0.5.0
docs.text: 0.4.0 0.5.0 Why observed_property a BERVO term when BERVO has one, otherwise a bridge_property: ID Always a bridge_property: ID, mapped to BERVO and others in observed_property.sssom.tsv, with labels and definitions in terms/bridge_property.tsv @valerie-autumn-skye's review (open question 4). Matching source property names against BERVO labels finds a term for a minority of them, mostly BERVO Concepts, so most measurements needed a bridge_property: ID anyway

docs.title: What changed in 0.4.0
docs.text:
After the first reviews of https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9 :

0.3.0 0.4.0 Why observed_time a full date-time with offset Year, year-month, date or date-time, plus observed_start_time and observed_end_time ESS-DIVE values come at coarser resolutions and some cover a period (open question 16) no treatment slot treatment ESS-DIVE: treatment is too important downstream to leave in the method text no unit basis unit_basis (text) ESS-DIVE's forthcoming unit basis; some bases cannot be written in UCUM (open question 3) source_system a free name the source's lakehouse registry ID when it has one, such as ber_registry:schema-jgi-gold the registry (https://github.com/doe-bridge/lakehouse-registry) already lists GOLD, NMDC, BASALT and ESS-DIVE MissingValueReasonEnum without unknown unknown added a source can say a value is unknown, which differs from leaving it empty (not_reported) value slot descriptions say which slots hold the value and which say something about it; measured covers spatial and temporal means open questions 13 and 15 R44 counted as handled R44 a known gap, with a problem example there is still no snapshot or version slot

docs.title: What changed from 0.2.0
docs.text:
0.2.0 0.3.0 Why Observation, with Measurement under it Measurement only One class to start (R01, R02) Values in a separate MeasurementValue / QuantityValue object under result Value slots directly on Measurement The 10/07 notes list type, value, raw value and unit as slots of one class; one measurement per value also loads as one table row observed_property must match ^bervo:BERVO_\d{7}$ Any identifier, or property_label Most GOLD and EMSL properties have no BERVO term yet (R38) (not in 0.2.0) Not taken: Measurement as a subclass of a QuantityValue class Open question 12 (R69). The first pass puts the value slots on Measurement directly instead exact_mappings to nmdc:QuantityValue and nmdc:AttributeValue close_mappings, slot by slot NMDC requires a unit from a closed list and has min/max; this module does not require a unit (issue 4, point 6) feature_of_interest commented out A reference slot only GOLD values cannot be told apart without the organism (issue 4, point 1); the classes it points to stay with the Samples, Projects, and Processes Modelling Squad Example BERVO IDs BERVO_0000001, BERVO_0000915, BERVO_0000123 Real terms or BRIDGE-issued IDs In BERVO release 2026-09-25 those three IDs are Ecosystem net radiation, Total phosphorus drainage below root zone, and an FePO4 equilibrium constant, not nitrate, total carbon and water temperature

Names were chosen to avoid the feature model's global slots in https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/5 (method, type, source, note), hence measurement_method and source_system. Both modules define numeric_value; this one uses double, and the feature model's Attribute.numeric_value is float, which should be made to match before both are merged.

docs.title: Examples by source
docs.text:
Source Valid examples What they show NMDC Measurement-001 to -003 text instead of a number, a range, a storage temperature that is a setting JGI GOLD Measurement-004 to -013 molar range, range plus optimum in one cell, mean ± SD with n, a category, not determined, two dimensions in one cell, unit taken from the column name, an unparseable value EMSL MONet Measurement-014, -015 0.0 plus a below-detection flag (recorded as missing, not zero), an outlier kept with its flag ORNL APPL Measurement-016, -017 a derived value with its method, a placeholder instead of a value BASALT Measurement-018 one measurement per analyte column of a wide table BASIN-3D Measurement-019 a mean with its time (the averaging window is not recorded; see known gaps) MIxS / NMDC misc_param Measurement-020 the free-text catch-all none (illustrative) Measurement-021 to -026 an identifier, instrument and less_than comparator; a categorical coded_value; a treatment, unit basis, month-only time and start and end times; a raw value containing a colon; unknown as the missing value reason; a year-only time

Each example's header says where it came from. Most cite a source file and row; Measurement-004 cites the GOLD organism ID, Measurement-019 is carried over from the 0.2.0 module, and Measurement-020 repeats the MIxS and NMDC misc_param examples. Those values were copied from their sources. Measurement-021 to -025, and the problem examples Measurement-004 and -005, were written to show a slot or a gap and say so in their headers.

docs.title: What the data showed
docs.text:
Read from the files in the hackathon shared drive on 2026-10-07:

  • GOLD: 48,308 of 530,610 organism rows (9.1%) carry any measurement value, which matches the roughly 9% given at the hackathon. Micrometres are written at least five ways (um, µm, μm, μm, micrometres); 24 rows in the diameter and length columns use the HTML entity.
  • EMSL MONet: below-detection values are stored as 0.0 with a flag in a parallel flag_* column. A parser that ignores the flag reads them as real zeros, which is why Measurement-014 records no number.
  • ORNL APPL: the unit, method and statistic sit on the variable definition, not on each value, so a loader has to copy them onto each measurement.
  • NMDC: the export flags 29,719 values with no raw value and 196 with a minimum greater than the maximum. Those counts come from the NMDC export's own problems column, not from this module.

docs.title: Open questions for the group
docs.text:
The first pass makes a provisional choice where it can. Each needs a group decision.

  1. Is a measurement a kind of observation, and when does an Observation class earn its place? (R03) Provisional: no Observation class. @valerie-autumn-skye: a measurement is an observation, and an interpretation such as "strain X is mesophilic" is an observation supported by measurements such as "strain X grows at 28 C" (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4273800445).
  2. Should raw_value be required? (R22) Provisional: recommended. A measurement needs some value or a reason it has none. @valerie-autumn-skye leans against requiring it, since it could add a lot of redundancy to large data sets or carry unintended meaning downstream (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4273685294).
  3. UCUM required, a closed unit list, or QUDT? (R30, R31) Provisional: UCUM code in printable ASCII, no list. @dschristianson asks what happens when there is no UCUM term (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4230751366), notes that ESS-DIVE uses QUDT, most of whose units map to UCUM (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4230965424), and that ESS-DIVE has a forthcoming unit_basis that further qualifies a unit, sometimes expressible in UCUM and sometimes not (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4230956454). 0.4.0 says what to do when a unit cannot be written in UCUM and adds an optional unit_basis. @valerie-autumn-skye recommends bridge_unit: identifiers mapped to UCUM terms and, where needed, other vocabularies, so the schema is not tied to one (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4273699901, https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4273505382). 0.5.0 keeps UCUM codes, since UCUM can write most units directly; a bridge_unit: ID would be added only for a unit UCUM has no unit for (such as PSU or FNU), and none of the examples needs one yet.
  4. How are BRIDGE property IDs issued, and under what prefix? (R38) 0.5.0: bridge_property: for every property, added by pull request with a label, a definition and mapping rows; the prefix does not resolve yet. Earlier question: should observed_property hold a BERVO ID when BERVO has the term, as this pass does, or always a bridge_property: ID mapped to BERVO and other vocabularies, as @valerie-autumn-skye recommends (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4273386207, https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4273779118)?
  5. Do measurements get BRIDGE-minted IDs on ingest? (R42) Provisional: measurement_id is optional. @dschristianson asks why it isn't just id (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4230719718). The central schema's id is an identifier, which LinkML makes required, so reusing it would make every measurement need one.
  6. How are related records grouped: a mean with its SD, replicates, the parts of one cell? (R52) Provisional: shared source_record_id and source_field.
  7. Who assigns coded_value for a scientist's label such as mesophilic, and how is it reviewed? (R18) @valerie-autumn-skye suggests an optional provenance field, such as source: PMID:29182670 or curation: GOLD (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4273734035).
  8. Numbers that are not quantities, such as grading scales and coefficients. (R24)
  9. A QA class, or is one quality_flag enough for now? (R64) @valerie-autumn-skye: quality_flag is enough for now (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4273737869).
  10. What do people want to search on? (R63) @valerie-autumn-skye considers this out of scope here and a question for the User Research team (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4273756898).
  11. (Raised while writing this pass.) Should a mapping to MIxS be exactMatch when MIxS defines the property of a sample and BERVO the property in general? The mapping file uses closeMatch for those.

  12. (Raised while reviewing this pass, R69.) Should Measurement be a subclass of QuantityValue, inheriting numeric_value, the minimum and maximum, and unit, and keeping NMDC's value structure? That treats a measurement as a kind of value. The first pass treats it as a record about a property that carries a value, with the value slots on Measurement and no QuantityValue class. @valerie-autumn-skye asks whether that would imply every measurement is numeric (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4273745478); it would, and categorical values (coded_value) are one reason the first pass did not do it.

  13. Is the line between a value and facts about a value clear? @dschristianson read coded_value (then named value_term) as the parsed form of a non-numeric value, like numeric_value for numbers, and asked how it relates to value_role and value_qualifier (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4230783915). That reading is right; 0.4.0 says so in the class comments and slot descriptions.

  14. Statistics come in kinds: temporal, spatial and measurement. Should statistic become a structure (type, statistic, number), possibly repeated on one measurement, with sample_size renamed (for example statistic_sample_number)? (@dschristianson, https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4230798043 and https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4230841807) The same structure could carry the period a value represents (daily, monthly, yearly), which observed time cannot always show (@dschristianson, https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#pullrequestreview-5519748477), or a separate sampling_period field could (@valerie-autumn-skye, https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4273300055).
  15. Which value_role fits a spatial mean of several measurements, which an earth scientist would call measured? (@dschristianson, https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4231116532) 0.4.0: measured, with the summary in statistic; derived is for a value of one property computed from others.
  16. observed_time is a full date-time. ESS-DIVE needs year, year-month and date resolutions, and records UTC only when a time is present. (@dschristianson, https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4230984199) 0.4.0 accepts all four resolutions and adds start and end times (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4272389263).
  17. For ESS-DIVE, source_record_id would likely combine a dataset DOI and a file PID. How should identifiers like that be combined and documented? (@dschristianson, https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4231015041)
  18. Should a generic attribute/value representation come first, with features and measurements built on it, as in bertron-schema's AttributeValue? (@ialarmedalien, https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/issues/11) This module is flat on purpose, following the 10/07 notes; that issue would decide nested or flat for the feature model and measurements together.
  19. For a sample-based measurement, the collection time often matters more than the lab measurement time. How should a measurement show that? (@dschristianson, https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4272389263) This overlaps the work of the Samples, Projects, and Processes Modelling Squad (https://doe-bridge.slack.com/archives/C0CAYBJ7CAF).
  20. Should the material measured (water, air, soil) be its own slot or part of the observed property? ESS-DIVE keeps it separate; CF Conventions fold it in (@dschristianson, https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#pullrequestreview-5519748477). BERVO release 2026-09-25 has both a plain Temperature and Air temperature and Soil temperature terms.
  21. Should time series go in this class or a separate one? (@dschristianson, https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#pullrequestreview-5519748477)
  22. gold: may be too narrow for JGI identifiers in general (@valerie-autumn-skye, https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4273817438).

Also from that review, all taken in 0.4.0: missing_value_reason probably needs an unknown option (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4231040002); feature_of_interest targets for ESS-DIVE would come from what @dschristianson called the Landscape/Physical Features working group, a module proposed in the 2026-10-07 BRIDGE DM notes (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4230737215); and the property_label fallback was welcomed (https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/pull/9#discussion_r4231133180).

docs.title: Known gaps and deferred work
docs.text:
• Time series (R50): tests/data/problem/invalid/Measurement-001.yaml fails today. Tracked in https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/issues/25.
  • A standard deviation reported as its own measurement (R15) and growth derived from several OD readings (R53) have no link to the measurements they belong with.
  • Nothing enforces maximum_numeric_value >= minimum_numeric_value. LinkML's equals_expression can state the comparison, but neither linkml-validate nor gen-sqltables checks it (LinkML 1.11.1, tested 2026-11-04), and NMDC's export has 196 inverted ranges. tests/data/problem/valid/Measurement-004.yaml validates anyway. Tracked in https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/issues/24.
  • A mean records no averaging window (hourly, daily), so Measurement-019 cannot say it is a daily mean (open question 14). Tracked in https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/issues/14.
  • Source lineage cannot tell revisions of the same source record apart. There is no snapshot or version slot yet (R44, tests/data/problem/valid/Measurement-005.yaml). Tracked in https://github.com/doe-bridge/bridge-central-schema/issues/23.
  • Sample, site and organism classes, replicates, and instrument records belong to the Samples, Projects, and Processes Modelling Squad (https://doe-bridge.slack.com/archives/C0CAYBJ7CAF) (R40, R48, R51).

docs.title: Class: GeneticModel
docs.text: A named genetic entity that organisms instantiate: a strain, genotype, cultivar, accession, line, isolate, ecotype or variant. Covers AGR's AffectedGenomicModel ("inbred strains, stocks, disease models and mutant genotypes") and MIAPPE's BiologicalMaterial (germplasm accessions and named lines). The subtype slot says which kind of entity a record claims to be, because communities draw the strain/genotype line differently rather than because the distinction is crisp.

docs.title: Induced
docs.text:
name: GeneticModel
description: 'A named genetic entity that organisms instantiate: a strain, genotype,
  cultivar, accession, line, isolate, ecotype or variant. Covers AGR''s AffectedGenomicModel
  ("inbred strains, stocks, disease models and mutant genotypes") and MIAPPE''s BiologicalMaterial
  (germplasm accessions and named lines). The subtype slot says which kind of entity
  a record claims to be, because communities draw the strain/genotype line differently
  rather than because the distinction is crisp.'
comments:
- At least one of full_name or symbol must be populated (carried over from the AGR
  AffectedGenomicModel rule).
- Strain versus genotype, as users mean them. A strain / line / cultivar / accession
  is a material lineage you can obtain and propagate (it has a stock center, a holding
  institute, parents). A genotype is a description of genetic composition (alleles,
  zygosity, background). A strain has a genotype; a genotype can be written down for
  an individual that belongs to no named lineage. Both NMDC and AGR collapsed the
  two in practice, and no current BER source records allele-level composition, so
  this straw person keeps one class with a subtype and leaves decomposition to has_genomic_components.
- 'GENO (checked 2026-11-10) makes the same split and is upfront about it: GENO:0000536
  genotype is "a specification of the genetic state of an organism" (an information
  artifact), while GENO:0000112 strain or breed is "a maximal collection of organisms
  of a single species that have been bred or experimentally manipulated with the goal
  of being genetically identical" (a collection of material entities; GENO even notes
  that two colonies with the same genotype maintained in different labs are different
  strains). So no single GENO term covers this class; the subtype values carry the
  GENO meanings instead, and an ontologically strict future revision would split GeneticModel
  along exactly that line. GENO has no term for cultivar or botanical variety; those
  meanings come from EFO, NCIT and TAXRANK.'
- 'Per-kingdom usage of subtype. Plants: cultivar, accession, line (RILs), variety,
  ecotype (MCPD ranks via MIAPPE infraspecificName). Animals: strain (mouse, rat),
  genotype (fish, fly). Microbes and fungi: strain, isolate; engineered strains are
  strains whose has_genomic_components lists the modifications; NCBI Taxonomy sometimes
  has strain-level taxa (e.g. E. coli K-12 MG1655, NCBITaxon:511145), in which case
  taxon points there and the species-level rollup comes from the taxonomy, not this
  schema. Viruses: variant, isolate.'
- Lakehouse join points. has_genomic_components is the intended JGI connection (gene
  / transcript / allele CURIEs). EMSL MONet connects at study/project level only;
  nothing genotype-shaped exists there.
- 'Survey of plant resources (2026-11-10; Gramene, TAIR, SorghumBase/ GRIN, Ensembl
  Plants, Phytozome/GOLD, ABRC, pennycress resources): none has a genotype entity.
  Allelic composition everywhere is an association (TAIR germplasm-to-allele rows
  carrying zygosity; Ensembl per-variant sample calls), which supports keeping GeneticModel
  name-level and deferring components. Two recurring splits this single class absorbs,
  recorded here so mappings stay honest: (1) the line versus the orderable stock (TAIR
  Germplasm vs Stock, ABRC stock records) - the stock side lands in the material_source_*
  block; (2) the line versus its genome assembly (Ensembl species databases, Phytozome
  genome releases, Gramene) - the assembly side lands in genome_assemblies. GOLD''s
  organism entity has a strain field and no cultivar field (cultivars go in strain),
  so GOLD organisms map to this class with subtype strain or cultivar as the source
  metadata indicates.'

      assembly (Gramene and Ensembl: one cultivar = one genome database with a GCA
      accession; Phytozome: genome release slugs; SorghumBase: per-line gene namespaces).

docs.title: Class: Measurement
docs.text: One value of one property of one thing, as reported by a source. A measurement may carry a number with a unit, a range, a summary statistic, a categorical term, or only the source text, and it may say why no value is present. The 2026-09-30 hackathon chose to start with this single class and add an Observation class only when data shows a need for one.

docs.title: Induced

name: Measurement
description: One value of one property of one thing, as reported by a source. A measurement
  may carry a number with a unit, a range, a summary statistic, a categorical term,
  or only the source text, and it may say why no value is present. The 2026-09-30
  hackathon chose to start with this single class and add an Observation class only
  when data shows a need for one.
comments:
- A measurement must carry at least one of raw_value, numeric_value, minimum_numeric_value,
  maximum_numeric_value, coded_value or missing_value_reason, so an empty measurement
  fails validation.
- A measurement names its property with exactly one of observed_property (an identifier)
  or property_label (free text). property_label is the catch-all for values whose
  property has no identifier yet, as MIxS misc_param, NMDC PropertyAssertion and BERtron
  Attribute allow.
- 'The value slots come in two groups. raw_value, numeric_value, minimum_numeric_value,
  maximum_numeric_value, unit and coded_value hold the value itself: raw_value as
  the source wrote it, the others as parsed from it (numeric_value for a number, coded_value
  for a category). comparator, statistic, standard_deviation, sample_size, value_role,
  value_qualifier and missing_value_reason say something about that value.'
- A source cell that holds several values (for example a width and a length) becomes
  several measurements that share source_record_id and source_field.

docs.title: Class: PhenotypicMeasurement
docs.text: A measurement of a phenotypic trait of an organism or observation unit: one trait value, produced by one method, at one time. Modeled on MIAPPE v1.2 Observed Variable (trait + method + scale) and on the ORNL APPL plant phenotyping exports, where one Observation row is one trait value from one imaging event.

docs.title: Induced
docs.text:
name: PhenotypicMeasurement
description: 'A measurement of a phenotypic trait of an organism or observation unit:
  one trait value, produced by one method, at one time. Modeled on MIAPPE v1.2 Observed
  Variable (trait + method + scale) and on the ORNL APPL plant phenotyping exports,
  where one Observation row is one trait value from one imaging event.'
comments:
- 'Deliberately thin. Measurement already carries what phenotyping needs: the trait''s
  name goes in observed_property or property_label, the method in measurement_method,
  the summary in statistic, the image-QC state in quality_flag, missing values in
  missing_value_reason, and computed traits (pixel counts times a calibration scale,
  such as APPL''s millimetre areas) in value_role derived. Only the trait-ontology
  hooks are new.'
- 'Phenotype versus measurement: a raw trait value (projected shoot area on one date,
  Fv/Fm from one fluorescence event) is a measurement and belongs here. An interpreted
  phenotype claim ("dwarf under high dose"), aggregated over many measurements, is
  a knowledge-level assertion and is deliberately NOT this class; value_role interpreted
  covers a single interpreted value, and a future Phenotype class referencing the
  measurements it derives from would cover the aggregate. Flagged as an open question
  on the genotype/strain straw person.'
- QC values that describe the measuring process rather than the organism (for example
  APPL's fc1.mask_coverage_pct segmentation coverage) should be plain Measurements,
  not PhenotypicMeasurements, so trait tables are not polluted with instrument diagnostics.
- 'A known APPL pitfall this model should not reproduce: events whose segmentation
  found no plant (empty_mask) store 0.0 instead of no value. Here that case keeps
  the source''s 0.0 in raw_value only, with missing_value_reason not_determined and
  quality_flag empty_mask, so no parsed numeric_value fabricates a size for a plant
  that was not seen.'

docs.title: ber-central-schema
docs.text:
The central BRIDGE schema for harmonized cross-BER data access. Defines shared base elements and composes domain modules (currently: measurements.yaml, genotype.yaml).

URI: https://w3id.org/ber-data/bridge-central-schema

docs.title: Slot: coded_value
docs.text: A categorical value as a code from an ontology or controlled vocabulary, parsed from raw_value the way numeric_value is parsed for a number, such as METPO:1000615 (mesophilic). The source wording stays in raw_value.

docs.title: Slot: comparator
docs.text: How the true value relates to numeric_value, for values reported as above or below a number, such as below a detection limit. When the source gives the limit as a number, record it in numeric_value with a comparator; when it gives no number, use missing_value_reason below_detection_limit instead.

docs.title: Slot: description
docs.text: A human-readable description for a thing

docs.title: Slot: feature_of_interest
docs.text: A reference to the thing whose property was measured: a sample, an organism, a site or plot, a stream. Only a reference: classes for samples belong to the Samples, Projects, and Processes Modelling Squad, and classes for sites, plots and other landscape features to the Landscape/Physical Features module proposed in the 2026-10-07 BRIDGE DM notes.

docs.title: Slot: full_name
docs.text: The one current full name for the genetic model.

docs.title: Slot: genetic_background
docs.text: The reference line or ecotype this model was made in or backcrossed to, such as Col-0 for a SALK T-DNA insertion line. Distinct from parent_models: a background is a reference, not a cross parent.

docs.title: Slot: genetic_model
docs.text: The named strain, genotype, cultivar, accession, line, isolate or variant this organism is an instance of.

docs.title: Slot: genetic_model_description
docs.text: A human-readable description of the genetic model.

docs.title: Slot: genetic_model_id
docs.text: Unique identifier for the genetic model. When the source assigns one (a ZFIN genotype ID, a germplasm accession ID), keep it; otherwise BRIDGE mints one on ingest.

docs.title: Slot: genome_assemblies
docs.text: Genome assembly or annotation releases of this model: INSDC assembly accessions (GCA_911865555.2 for pennycress MN106-Ref) or portal release identifiers (Phytozome Tarvensevar_MN106_v4_1, Ensembl production names such as oryza_sativa_mh63). The scope anchor for has_genomic_components.

docs.title: Slot: genus
docs.text: Genus part of the organism name, per standard nomenclature.

docs.title: Slot: has_genomic_components
docs.text: References to the genomic parts that make up this model: gene, transcript, allele or construct CURIEs. A hook, not a structure; see comments.

docs.title: Slot: id
docs.text: A unique identifier for a thing

docs.title: Slot: instrument
docs.text: The instrument or sensor that produced the value.

docs.title: Slot: material_source_accession_name
docs.text: Registered accession or variety name in the source collection.

docs.title: Slot: material_source_accession_number
docs.text: Unique identifier for the accession within the source genebank or collection, e.g. W95115_inra.

docs.title: Slot: material_source_doi
docs.text: DOI of the material source.

docs.title: Slot: material_source_institute_code
docs.text: FAO WIEWS code (or laboratory acronym) of the institute holding the material, e.g. FRA09.

docs.title: Slot: material_source_institute_name
docs.text: Name of the institute holding the material.

docs.title: Slot: material_source_other_identifiers
docs.text: Other identifiers known for this material source, as key:value pairs when the source provides them.

docs.title: Slot: maximum_numeric_value
docs.text: The upper end of a range, or the upper bound of a one-sided value.

docs.title: Slot: measurement_id
docs.text: An identifier for this measurement, when the source has one or BRIDGE mints one on ingest. Optional, because many sources (ESS-DIVE among them) do not identify individual measurements.

docs.title: Slot: measurement_method
docs.text: How the value was obtained: a protocol name, a method reference, or the source's companion method field (for example an NMDC ph_meth value).

docs.title: Slot: member_of_populations
docs.text: Named panels, populations or collections this model belongs to, such as the Sorghum Association Panel, the 1001 Genomes collection, or a stock-center set. Free text or CURIE as the source provides.

docs.title: Slot: minimum_numeric_value
docs.text: The lower end of a range, or the lower bound of a one-sided value.

docs.title: Slot: missing_value_reason
docs.text: Why no usable value is present. Sources often write these as text (not determined) or as sentinel numbers (-9999); record the source text in raw_value.

docs.title: Slot: mutagen
docs.text: The mutagen applied to create this model, such as EMS, X-rays, fast neutron or T-DNA insertion, when it is a mutant line.

docs.title: Slot: name
docs.text: A human-readable name for a thing

docs.title: Slot: numeric_value
docs.text: A single number parsed from raw_value.

docs.title: Slot: observed_end_time
docs.text: The end of the period a value covers. Same format as observed_time.

docs.title: Slot: observed_property
docs.text: The property that was measured, as a BRIDGE property identifier (bridge_property:).

docs.title: Slot: observed_start_time
docs.text: The start of the period a value covers, for sources that report a start and an end instead of one time. Same format as observed_time.

docs.title: Slot: observed_time
docs.text: When the property was observed, in ISO 8601 at whatever resolution the source gives: a year (2021), a year and month (2021-06), a date (2021-06-15), or a date-time with a UTC offset (2021-06-15T14:30:00-07:00). A time of day must carry an offset; a date or coarser does not.

docs.title: Slot: organism_id
docs.text: Unique identifier for the organism record.

docs.title: Slot: organism_name
docs.text: A human-readable name or label for the organism.

docs.title: Slot: parent_models
docs.text: Parental lineages: AGR parental populations, or MIAPPE's "mother_accession X father_accession" convention for material derived from a cross.

docs.title: Slot: pedigree
docs.text: The pedigree exactly as the source wrote it, in cross notation, for example ((SC120-6*Tx7000)Tx7000)-10-4-6-1-1-1-bk (a GRIN sorghum pedigree). parent_models holds the references that resolve to records; this keeps the full string, which usually does not resolve.

docs.title: Slot: property_label
docs.text: The name of the measured property as free text, for values whose property has no BRIDGE identifier yet. Use observed_property instead whenever an identifier exists.

docs.title: Slot: quality_flag
docs.text: A flag from the source or from BRIDGE curation, such as needs_review for a value that could not be parsed.

docs.title: Slot: raw_value
docs.text: The value exactly as it appeared at the source, including its unit text, ranges, qualifiers and any non-ASCII characters. Never edited. The other value slots are parsed from it.

docs.title: Slot: sample_size
docs.text: How many readings, replicates or individuals a statistic summarizes.

docs.title: Slot: secondary_identifiers
docs.text: Identifiers for the same entity in other collections (EBI BioSamples, germplasm databases, stock centers).

docs.title: Slot: source_field
docs.text: The source field, column or slot the value came from, named as the source names it.

docs.title: Slot: source_record_id
docs.text: The identifier of the source record the value came from, in the source's own format. The schema does not impose a format.

docs.title: Slot: source_system
docs.text: The system the value came from. Use the BER lakehouse registry entry (https://github.com/doe-bridge/lakehouse-registry) for the source's schema when it has one, such as ber_registry:schema-jgi-gold; otherwise the system's name, such as BASIN-3D (USGS).

docs.title: Slot: species
docs.text: Specific epithet part of the organism name.

docs.title: Slot: standard_deviation
docs.text: The standard deviation reported with a mean, in the same unit.

docs.title: Slot: statistic
docs.text: The summary statistic that numeric_value reports, when the source value summarizes several readings or individuals.

docs.title: Slot: subtype
docs.text: Which kind of named genetic entity this record claims to be. Extends AGR's strain / genotype / fish vocabulary with the MCPD infraspecific ranks MIAPPE uses for plants and with microbial and viral usage.

docs.title: Slot: symbol
docs.text: The one current accepted symbol, e.g. CB1370 (a C. elegans strain) or a zebrafish genotype symbol.

docs.title: Slot: synonyms
docs.text: Non-preferred names for the genetic model, any type.

docs.title: Slot: taxon
docs.text: Taxonomic classification as an NCBITaxon CURIE. On GeneticModel this may be a strain-level taxon when NCBI has one; on Organism it is usually species-level.

docs.title: Slot: trait_entity_term
docs.text: Ontology accession for the part of the organism the trait is about (Plant Ontology for plants), for example PO:0009006 shoot system.

docs.title: Slot: trait_term
docs.text: Ontology accession for the phenotypic trait as a whole (Trait Ontology, Crop Ontology), when one exists. The trait's name goes in observed_property or property_label as for any measurement; this slot adds the trait-ontology mapping MIAPPE asks for. In the APPL corpus 0 of 512 variables carry any trait accession, so this is optional and expected to be sparse.

docs.title: Slot: treatment
docs.text: The experimental treatment applied to the thing measured, such as a warming or nitrogen addition plot, kept apart from measurement_method because downstream users filter and compare on it.

docs.title: Slot: unit
docs.text: The unit as a UCUM code, written in printable ASCII (for example um, not µm). Leave empty for values without a unit, such as pH. The source's own spelling stays in raw_value. UCUM is a grammar rather than a fixed list, so most units can be written even when no common code exists, and annotations in braces cover counted things ({cells}/g). When a unit cannot be written in UCUM, leave unit empty and keep the source's unit in raw_value. Many units from QUDT (used by ESS-DIVE) carry a UCUM code (qudt:ucumCode) that can go here.

docs.title: Slot: unit_basis
docs.text: What the unit is expressed relative to, when the unit alone does not say, such as dry weight. Some bases fit UCUM annotations (mg{C}/L); this slot is for those that do not. Free text until examples settle a vocabulary.

docs.title: Slot: value_qualifier
docs.text: A qualifier the source attaches to the value, such as an optimum (optimal growth at 10 MPa).

docs.title: Slot: value_role
docs.text: Whether the value was measured, set as an experimental condition, or assigned by a person interpreting other measurements.

docs.text: ID Point Raised by Source Where it went R01 Start with one class and add structure when data needs it; build a union straw-person and see what each source can conform to. @mslarae13 brainstorm drawing Measurement is the only class R02 Lean towards one concept for now rather than separate Observation and Measurement classes. BRIDGE DM team DM notes 10/07 Measurement is the only class; Observation and the MeasurementValue/QuantityValue split from 0.2.0 are removed R04 We may not have enough data recording observation properties to justify an Observation class. @caufieldjh brainstorm drawing no Observation class R05 JGI examples would split between Observation and Measurement, and users may want to search them together. @valerie-autumn-skye brainstorm drawing one class, so categorical and numeric values are searched together (valid Measurement-008) R06 The core parts are a type, a value, a raw value and a unit. BRIDGE DM team DM notes 10/07 observed_property (alias measurement_type), numeric_value, raw_value, unit R07 Make a schema, then see whether each source can map up to it; feedback loop up to a cutoff date. @corilo, @turbomam Zoom chat this first pass; examples from GOLD, NMDC, EMSL MONet, ORNL APPL, BASALT and BASIN-3D R08 Generic property/value model (BASIN-3D, BERtron) or named-property model (NMDC, BASALT)? @sierra-moxon intro slides generic, one Measurement per value; a wide source becomes one record per column (valid Measurement-018) R09 Data is too diverse for named attributes; averages over time and space must be captured with the measurements. @dschristianson Hackathon Notes generic observed_property plus statistic R10 A catch-all for values that fit nowhere else, as MIxS misc_param, NMDC PropertyAssertion and BERtron Attribute provide. @turbomam first-pass review property_label (free text) as the alternative to observed_property (valid Measurement-020) R11 Ranges, such as 0.16-0.22. @valerie-autumn-skye Zoom chat minimum_numeric_value, maximum_numeric_value (valid Measurement-002, -004, -012) R12 Split ranges into high and low fields. JGI Report Out tab minimum_numeric_value, maximum_numeric_value R13 Two dimensions in one field (cell diameter and cell length), or are these two measurements? @valerie-autumn-skye Zoom chat two Measurement records sharing source_record_id and source_field (valid Measurement-010, -011) R14 Uncertainty, such as 1.870 +/- 0.568 um (mean +/- standard deviation for 63 cells). @valerie-autumn-skye Zoom chat statistic, standard_deviation, sample_size (valid Measurement-007) R16 Qualitative values, such as circumneutral pH. @valerie-autumn-skye Zoom chat raw_value plus value_role interpreted; coded_value for an ontology term (valid Measurement-008) R17 Instantiate categorical values (mesophilic) as observations. @turbomam brainstorm drawing coded_value on Measurement, since there is one class R19 Context attached to a value, such as Optimal 10MPa or "for optimal growth". @valerie-autumn-skye Zoom chat value_qualifier (optimum, tolerated) (valid Measurement-005, -006) R20 Split non-measurement qualifiers (such as "optimal") into their own field. JGI Report Out tab value_qualifier R21 Are some of these experimental settings rather than measurements (grew at 5 degrees for 2 hours)? Things measured versus things intended. @turbomam brainstorm drawing value_role setting (valid Measurement-003) R23 Implicit NA and sentinel values (9999 meaning not in range); "not determined"; below detection. @caufieldjh, @valerie-autumn-skye Zoom chat missing_value_reason, comparator (valid Measurement-001, -009, -014, -017) R25 Not all numbers have units (pH, % salinity). @caufieldjh, @valerie-autumn-skye, @ialarmedalien Zoom chat unit is optional (valid Measurement-008) R26 Malformed values (107.55.82) and unitless salinity (8258) in GOLD. @valerie-autumn-skye Hackathon Notes raw_value kept, no number, quality_flag needs_review (valid Measurement-013) R27 Flag ambiguous records for review. @valerie-autumn-skye Hackathon Notes quality_flag R28 Retain original values (NMDC TextValue approach) while parsing typed numbers. @valerie-autumn-skye Hackathon Notes raw_value beside the parsed slots R29 Allow non-Latin characters in units? um, µm and μ all appear. Require or coerce to UTF-8? Normalize with reasonable effort. @turbomam, @caufieldjh, @valerie-autumn-skye Zoom chat raw_value keeps the source bytes; unit must be printable ASCII (invalid Measurement-002) R32 Separate the unit description from a unit ontology code. JGI Report Out tab unit holds the code; the source's description stays in raw_value R34 BERVO as the dictionary of measured properties; BERVO term coverage for plant phenotypes is partial. @sierra-moxon, @caufieldjh Zoom chat observed_property is always a bridge_property identifier, mapped to BERVO when BERVO has the term R35 Map to other vocabularies with SKOS-style mappings rather than importing terms (MIREOT). @caufieldjh Zoom chat mappings/observed_property.sssom.tsv R36 Where does MIxS fit, in BERVO mappings? @sierra-moxon intro slides MIxS terms are mapping targets in mappings/observed_property.sssom.tsv, never the observed_property value R37 KBase defined a measurement as the value of a variable_id (from a controlled vocabulary) under specified conditions. @ialarmedalien Zoom chat observed_property (alias variable); conditions through value_role and value_qualifier R39 Feature of interest (plot of land, sample, organism) and its type; there are nested features. @sierra-moxon, @valerie-autumn-skye Hackathon Notes feature_of_interest as a reference only; the classes it points to are deferred to the Samples, Projects, and Processes Modelling Squad R41 Not all observations are tied to a sample (air temperature at a field site). @mslarae13 Zoom chat feature_of_interest accepts any identifier, or none (valid Measurement-017) R43 If each measurement is a specific event, it is not a NamedThing; NamedThing works against a domain hierarchy. @caufieldjh, @turbomam Zoom chat Measurement does not inherit from NamedThing R45 Review the exact_mappings to NMDC QuantityValue and AttributeValue until the constraints match; add NMDC's minimum and maximum fields. @valerie-autumn-skye issue 4 mappings to nmdc are close_mappings; minimum and maximum added R46 Method. NMDC pairs some slots with a method slot (ph with ph_meth, but no temp_meth); ESS-DIVE plans to add method; where does "how" live? @bmeluch, @dschristianson, @sierra-moxon Zoom chat measurement_method (named to avoid the feature model's method slot) R47 BASALT has an instrument class. @bmeluch Zoom chat instrument (text for now) R49 Time, with UTC offsets. @dschristianson Hackathon Notes observed_time, observed_start_time, observed_end_time (ISO 8601; an offset whenever a time of day is given) R54 Derived measurement columns (APPL visual transformer outputs); measurements are modalities. @pranjan77 Hackathon Notes value_role derived (valid Measurement-016); modality is deferred to the Phenotype/genotype/strain working group (new in the 2026-11-03 BRIDGE DM notes) R55 Complicated experimental conditions entered under "other", such as "prescribed burn every 3-4 years". @bmeluch Zoom chat fire_return_interval as a range, with treatment for the prescribed part (valid Measurement-027). The burn events themselves are not measurements R61 METPO for categorical microbial traits. @caufieldjh, @turbomam Zoom chat coded_value accepts METPO terms; METPO is a mapping target for cell length and growth temperature R62 Every element should have a text description, and something should check that the description agrees with the schema and the data. not recorded Hackathon Notes every class, slot, enum and value in measurements.yaml has a description; the agreement check is not built
